Performers
The Griller String Quartet (string quartet), Sidney Griller (violin), Jack O’Brien (violin), Philip Burton (viola), Colin Hampton (cello) Documented

The two photographed disc labels explicitly name all four players and their instruments. They do not label the violin chairs first and second; the dossier does not expand their order into a chair attribution.

[1] [3]
Work version
Original quartet scoring; movement III. The Archive’s combined III–IV designation is disputed. Disputed: sources disagree

The exact selected 1092.62-second MP3 is retained without truncation or substitution. Its analysed structure supports the five alternating spans of III, at approximately 0, 214, 340, 558 and 686 seconds, followed by slow music through the endpoint. The required report does not establish an A major march or the IV–V link. Supplementary upper-band inspection finds an F-centred ending; verifier VerH independently checked the selected file’s final37.6s against the score and also found the F ending of III, not IV’s dominant recitative. These are score/audio-feature correspondences, not an aural or complete bar-aligned certification. No IV boundary or IV listening prose is invented. Performing edition, cuts, repeat observance and the completeness of the final played release remain unestablished.

  • III–IV combined, as asserted by the Archive filename and catalogue metadata
  • III only, supported by the selected file’s five-span design and independently checked F-centred endpoint

Recorded
Unknown Unknown

1952 is the Archive’s catalogue/publication year, not an established session year. The sleeve’s 1951 copyright notice is for the printed package and does not date the session. No dated session ledger or independently matched master history was found in the consulted sources.

[1] [2] [3]
Place
Unknown Unknown

Made in England on the labels establishes manufacture, not recording location. The Archive’s Cebu scan/rip station and the ensemble’s name do not identify a session venue.

[2] [3]
Label
London Records, ffrr long-playing microgroove issue Documented

London, ffrr and 33⅓ rpm are visible on the labels. The sleeve names The London Gramophone Corporation, New York.

[1] [2] [3]
Catalogue
LLP 318 Documented

The Archive and its Discogs-derived catalogue metadata give 1952. The viewed rear sleeve reads Copyright 1951 by The London Gramophone Corporation. A sleeve copyright year is not proof of first sound-recording publication in that year; 1952 is retained as the source’s catalogue year rather than silently resolving the difference. Both are earlier than 1963.

[1] [2] [3] [4]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 1, label No.1: ABL.597 — movements I and II, not selected, Side 2, label No.2: ABL.598 — movements III, IV and V; the selected digital track is labelled III–IV, but its combined-movement identity is disputed Documented

The ABL identifiers were read on the photographed labels, where they are printed upside down below the personnel. They are label master identifiers, not inspected run-out inscriptions. Take numbers, stamper suffixes and session-master correspondence remain unknown.

[3] [2] [4]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP digitisation Documented

This account is explicitly credited in ripping_operator. The separate catalogue/uploader account is not credited as the audio transfer engineer. Collection membership identifies the Boston Public Library vinyl collection; it does not establish the original recording venue. No personal-name expansion or mastering credit is inferred.

[2]
Transfer date
23 September 2021 Documented

The explicit ripping_date field is 20210923105311. This is an analogue-disc digitisation date, unlike the August catalogue scan date, September added date or August 2023 derivative timestamp. Time zone is not established.

[2]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 turntable and Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; ArchiveCD 2.2.57lp; VBR MP3 segment derived from side-2 FLAC. Documented

The lineage and ripping-software fields state the hardware/software chain. The side-2 FLAC carries ‘Processed by SoX’; the item’s final segmentation is 7.434–⁠1100.006 seconds of that side capture for III–IV. That is a digital cut range, not score alignment. Stylus calibration beyond the named cartridge, equalisation settings, restoration, de-clicking and pitch/speed correction are not documented; no tuning value is supplied.

[2]
Composition rights
Underlying composition and the nineteenth-century Breitkopf & Härtel quartet score are public domain. Documented

The quartet was composed in 1825; Beethoven died in 1827. The consulted Beethovens Werke engraving, plate B.51, is catalogued as the 1863 edition and Public Domain. This does not clear an unidentified later performing edition or the sleeve author’s prose.

[8] [7] [9] [11]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis only: the recording was published before 1963; US status is not established. Documented

The admitted basis is eu-published-before-1963, using the Archive’s 1952 catalogue date for this identified London LLP318 issue. The printed sleeve carries a 1951 copyright notice, corroborating an early-1950s package but not independently establishing the first publication year of the sound recording. A recording published by 1952 had exhausted the ordinary EU 50-year phonogram term before 1 November 2013; the 2011 extension applies to recordings still protected on that date. This is territorial, not a Creative Commons grant or worldwide clearance. The US 1947–⁠1956 term is longer, and no US public-domain claim is made. The Archive item supplies no separate recording licence; availability online and Beethoven’s public-domain composition are not the admission basis.

Ludwig van Beethoven, String Quartet No.15, Op.132, III; Archive filename’s III–IV combined designation disputed. The Griller String Quartet. London Records LLP318, catalogued 1952; session date and place unknown. Internet Archive/Boston Public Library vinyl collection, digitised 23 September 2021. Territorial EU public-domain recording basis; US status unestablished. Rights statement
